lines.text: So far you have used AI. Today you will train one yourself, with no code at all.
Machine learning means a computer learns from examples instead of rules.
Show it many photos of paper and plastic, and it learns to tell them apart.
Each group you want it to learn is called a class, like “Paper”, “Plastic” and “Nothing”.
The photos you give it are the data.
More varied data usually makes a smarter model.
Training is when the computer studies your examples.
Testing is when you show it new things it has never seen.
A model is only as good as your test says.
Every model makes mistakes, even one that looks perfect at first.
If you only trained with blue bottles, a green bottle may confuse it.
Write down what fails and why in your data diary.
Open Teachable Machine and start an image project — you do not need an account.
Make one class for each thing you want it to recognise, and name them clearly.
Add lots of example photos to each class, then click Train Model.
Now hold up new objects in the preview and watch the confidence bars move.
A real tester tries to break the model with new objects, new backgrounds and dim light.
Write every test in your data diary, then look for a pattern in the mistakes.
The learner describes the problem to the AI helper, without sharing any personal details.
The helper suggests the model learned the light and background, not just the object.
That is a great idea to test — so we add more varied photos and train again.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
